IDEAS home Printed from https://ideas.repec.org/a/pal/palcom/v13y2026i1d10.1057\_s41599-025-06268-8.html. # A novel deep learning framework with advanced feature engineering for hate speech detection in accented Malayalam speech. This study introduces a comprehensive deep learning framework for detecting hate speech in accented Malayalam speech, integrating advanced feature engineering, class balancing, and robustness evaluation. These results confirm that the integration of balanced learning, multi-level validation, and robustness evaluation significantly enhances the reliability of hate speech detection in accented and low-resource Malayalam speech, establishing a transferable framework for multilingual content moderation. To address potential overfitting and data leakage risks noted in the initial evaluations, this extended study introduces cross-dataset validation, detailed speaker-independent and hold-out testing, and rigorous noise robustness analysis. results.content: This study introduces a comprehensive deep learning framework for detecting hate speech in accented Malayalam speech, integrating advanced feature engineering, class balancing, and robustness evaluation. To bridge this gap, the initial phase of our research focused on building a baseline hate speech detection model for accented Malayalam using carefully engineered acoustic features and a customized one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D CNN). 2022 International Conference on Computing, Communication, Security and Intelligent Systems (IC3SIS), pp 1–6")) investigated hate speech detection in English-Malayalam code-mixed text using BERT embeddings, demonstrating the effectiveness of transformer-based models in capturing contextual nuances in low-resource settings; however, their work focused exclusively on text. This experiment demonstrates that combining oversampling techniques with both deep learning and tree-based models provides reliable and high-performance hate speech detection. Our proposed work, utilizing CNN, SVM, and Random Forest models, demonstrates superior performance on accented Malayalam speech, achieving an F1-score of 0.966 (on noisy datasets) and an AUC of 0.998 under rigorous speaker-independent and hold-out validation settings.
